open_points.subject: A21 concurrency review of A17 startup
open_points.text: a start serving nothing until every check passed and binding each listener exclusively (A17)
open_points.question: When are listeners bound relative to the other startup checks: before them but kept non-serving, or only after every other check has passed?
options: Bind every listener first, keep all of them non-serving, then run the remaining checks.
Run every non-binding check first, then bind the listeners exclusively.
Treat exclusive binding as one of the checks, with an explicitly specified position in the check order.
open_points.default_guess: Bind every listener first without accepting traffic, then run the remaining checks, so another process cannot invalidate a preflight check by taking an address.

witness.initial: All configured listener addresses are free and startup has at least one other check that takes time.
events: While A is running its checks, Registry process B attempts to bind the same listeners.
outcomes: A already holds the listeners without serving; B is refused, and A serves only after its remaining checks pass.
A has not bound yet; B acquires the listeners, and A later refuses startup when its binding step fails.
witness.observer: The owner starting or diagnosing the two Registry processes.

open_points.subject: A21 concurrency review of multiple A17 listeners
open_points.question: If concurrent starts split a set of listener bindings between them, must acquisition be all-or-nothing, and must every partially acquired listener be released immediately when the start cannot acquire the rest?
options: Serialize or otherwise acquire the complete listener set all-or-nothing so one start can own every listener.
Allow sequential acquisition, but on any failure release every listener acquired by that start and refuse it.
Allow a failed or still-checking start to retain listeners it acquired, while serving nothing.
open_points.default_guess: Acquire sequentially under a startup lock and release the entire partial set immediately on failure.

witness.initial: The deployment has two configured listeners, both initially free.
events: A attempts listener 2 and B attempts listener 1.
outcomes: Partial acquisitions are rolled back; both starts refuse and both listeners become free.
Startup acquisition is serialized or atomic; one process obtains both listeners and may serve after all checks pass.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees either a running Registry or two refused starts despite both listeners having initially been free.
